question: Consider the following Java code: ```java interface Flyable { void fly(); } abstract class Bird { abstract void sing(); } class Sparrow extends Bird implements Flyable { void sing() { System.out.println("Tweet"); } public void fly() { System.out.println("Flap"); } } ``` Which statement about this code is correct?
answers: It won't compile because a class cannot both extend a class and implement an interface
It compiles because a class can extend one class and implement multiple interfaces
It won't compile because fly() must be declared abstract in Flyable
It won't compile because sing() needs the public modifier in Sparrow
